revenue_accrual_inconsistent.notes: Revenue is real and goes to a treasury the token holders vote on. That is better than CFG or HUMA, where the token sees nothing. But it is small and shrinking: about $514k a month, or ≈ 130x price-to-sales. **4**, so the gate is not tripped.

People pay real money to use Bitcoin, but it is small next to a $1.3T asset (~0.006% a year), and none of it reaches holders. Miners rely on new coins for ~99% of their income; that subsidy halves again in 2028. BTC's value case is scarcity, not cash flow, so it scores low on this section by design.

The business is real and growing, and it earns more than most tokens on this list. The token gets almost none of it: holders received about **$1 for every $225** the company kept, and nothing obliges the company to keep buying. That is better than a token with no business (QNT scored 4 for an optional, unmeasured sink), so **5**, but well short of a pass.
Yes, it makes money, and some of it is used to buy LINK. Annualised revenue is ~$65M on a $7B cap.

The company makes real, audited money and is profitable. The token gets no share of it. Paying in QNT is optional and nothing forces buying, so ~$2.3B of market cap sits on top of a ~£11.5M-a-year software business that can be paid in dollars. Better than a token with no business behind it (4, not 3). Fusion gas is the one direct token sink, and it is unmeasured.

## 💰 Revenue — Does it make money? · 7/10 · ✅ PASS - Yield comes from reinsurance premiums and collateral return: SOFR + 250 bps off-chain, sUSDe + 250 bps on-chain ([About reUSD](https://docs.re.xyz/products/about-reusd)). NAV is up 11% since launch.

The business is real and cheap on a sales multiple, but the token has no claim on revenue and no live buyback. SOLV's uses are governance, staking and fee discounts. **4**: better than a zero-revenue token, but it does not pass.

Real revenue from institutional lending, cheap relative to the token's market cap, and a written rule that routes part of it into buybacks.
